# R9 offline replay: draw and hold on the saved probabilities (generated by scripts/r9-held-replay.ts; do not edit)

Registration: `docs/staging/r9-prereg.md` §7. **Predictions, not results.** First order: the asks, menus and probabilities are those of the saved top-pick runs of R4b's loop test (seeds 21 and 5, five focal animals and five days each); a different choice would have led to other states. Rates are per animal and day. Draws and held draws are means over 30 decode salts (the range across salts in brackets where shown). "Act changes" here are changes of the applied option from one ask to the next, a count on the receipts; the loop's own count (`changes` in the day rows) also sees acts the gate keeps, arrivals and the rules' fallbacks, so the two are not the same instrument.

## 1. The sceptic's figures, recomputed

His rule: the noise of a held draw is kept until the held option is missing from the menu or more than 60 minutes have passed since the animal's last ask. His figures (review of 10 October): a held draw overturned at 21 to 25% of re-asks for the first adapter and 27 to 34% for the third; the option chosen last missing from the next menu at 24 to 28% of asks; third adapter, gate off, 32 to 44 trips begun a day under the held draw (top pick 44 to 63) and 9.6 to 10 with the gate on; act changes with the gate on 29 to 31 (top pick), 34 to 35 (fresh draw), 24 to 25 (held draw).

| Saved arm | seed | asks a day | previous pick missing from the next menu | held draw overturned (share of re-asks with it on the menu) | act changes a day: top pick | fresh draw | held draw | trips begun a day: top pick | fresh draw | held draw |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| first adapter (`r4-rules-state`), gate on | 21 | 54.8 | 30.0% | 23.7% | 30.5 | 35.0 | 23.4 | 2.0 | 4.6 | 3.0 |
| first adapter (`r4-rules-state`), gate on | 5 | 53.1 | 28.9% | 23.5% | 29.0 | 33.8 | 22.1 | 2.5 | 4.8 | 2.9 |
| third adapter (`r4c-rules-state`), gate on | 21 | 64.8 | 41.5% | 30.8% | 42.0 | 47.9 | 37.1 | 13.8 | 12.1 | 9.8 |
| third adapter (`r4c-rules-state`), gate on | 5 | 61.8 | 45.1% | 33.7% | 43.4 | 47.0 | 36.9 | 13.8 | 11.5 | 9.5 |
| first adapter, gate off | 21 | 103.0 | 24.7% | 21.8% | 52.7 | 65.7 | 40.3 | 5.4 | 9.3 | 5.7 |

| third adapter, gate off | 21 | 232.8 | 39.8% | 27.1% | 144.4 | 172.9 | 133.5 | 63.2 | 48.7 | 42.9 |
| third adapter, gate off | 5 | 157.9 | 45.5% | 26.0% | 98.2 | 115.0 | 89.9 | 44.0 | 36.6 | 31.8 |

Two differences from his script. (1) There, an option that left the menu and came back inside an epoch was given new noise; here an option's noise is fixed by its key for the whole epoch (the decode of prereg §1), so a returning option cannot re-roll: this moves the overturned share. (2) There, every opening of an epoch counted as an act change (and as a trip begun when the option was a trip), also when the option taken was the one held before (an opening after 60 minutes); here a change is counted only when the applied option changes: this lowers the held draw's act changes by less than one a day and moves no other column at the precision shown. With both changes made in a copy of his script it gives the figures above. His "missing from the next menu" was stated as one range; the column above gives it per arm, over every pair of consecutive asks of an animal.

## 2. This stage's epochs (the predictions for the arms)

The `act` epoch of every ask is the one step 0 recorded while it replayed the saved run through the loop (it opens at an animal's first ask, when its act was replaced or it arrived, at an interrupt, or after a fallback to the rules); `block` is the half hour of the ask. A **re-ask** is an ask inside an epoch that is already open: only there can holding differ from drawing afresh. `whole` (exploratory; prereg §10, amendment A2) is the act through interrupts: an ask the saved run opened at an interrupt alone, its act still going, is counted as a re-ask.

Both seeds pooled (50 animal-days an arm).

| Saved arm | asks a day | epochs opened a day: first | act replaced | arrived | interrupt | of those, the act was also replaced | after a fallback | re-asks a day | re-asks as a share of asks | at a re-ask the option applied last (the top pick, as run) is missing |

The applied option changes at a re-ask with the option applied last still on the menu (for `held` this is "the held draw is overturned"). The last two columns: the share of re-asks at which the option applied last is not on the menu at all, by epoch rule. For the top pick these are the saved run's own acts and menus. For a held draw the walk asks about an option the saved run did not apply, on the menus the top pick's states produced, so its figure under `act` and `whole` is first order and likely too high (in a run the animal would be doing that act); under `block` the option is missing as often for the top pick itself, because the act ends before the half hour does:

## 3. Model time of the saved arms (the estimate for a new arm)

A new arm of the same adapter, seed and gate asks the model about as often as the saved one at first order, so the saved arm's model time is the estimate (five animals, five days, one seed; both seeds summed in the last column).
